title: Keep web editor text and cursor stable in multiline comments
description: Typing or navigating inside multiline comments in the web interface causes the displayed editor contents to diverge from the entered text, making editing impractical. Identify the editor state/highlighting feedback loop and preserve text plus selection during comment edits.
acceptance_criteria: Typing, deleting, selecting, and moving the cursor inside and around multiline comments keeps the visible text synchronized with the editor value; automated frontend regression coverage passes.
notes: Restored hql-comment highlighting after confirming the interface had not been rebuilt during earlier testing. COMMENT and MULTILINECOMMENT both map to the comment category; Unicode-safe offsets and per-line range splitting remain, and styling is color-only. npm test (4) and lint pass; npm run build passes tsc but the Linux runner's current node_modules still lacks @rollup/rollup-linux-arm64-gnu.

title: Fan out SCOT relationship macros across multiple IDs
description: Join optimization produces multiple alert id values for the alert/entity relationship. The path-aware SCOT compiler currently rejects multi-value IDs, so joining Alerts to Entities returns no rows instead of issuing one relationship request per alert.
acceptance_criteria: N unique alert IDs resolve to N /api/v1/alert/{id}/entity requests, duplicate IDs are fetched once, rows are combined for downstream join/filter evaluation, and zero IDs still make zero requests.
notes: Extended relationship path compilation to retain a deduplicated, numerically ordered set of path values. OR/list IDs now resolve to multiple concrete paths, while contradictory AND predicates still invalidate the relationship. SCOT fetches each unique path once and combines validated result rows before downstream filtering/joining. Added a full query regression with 11 alert rows and 10 unique IDs, asserting exactly 10 relationship requests and joined results. Validation: 183 focused SCOT tests pass; full suite 527 passed, 2 skipped, with the same 8 unrelated InstructionSet fake-upstream failures.
close_reason: Implemented multi-ID relationship fan-out with deduplication and result aggregation.

title: Add SCOT alert entity relationship macro
description: Support database('scot').index('alert').macro('entity') as a lazy relationship source. Consume an applicable id equality into /api/v1/alert/{id}/entity, keep unrelated filters for local HQL evaluation, and avoid HTTP when no usable id exists.
acceptance_criteria: The macro route validates against the checked-in OpenAPI schema; id == 1 requests /api/v1/alert/1/entity; non-path predicates remain locally evaluated; missing, invalid, ambiguous, or non-equality IDs return an empty named dataset without a request; offline compiler/database tests pass.
notes: Added an OpenAPI-validated SCOT relationship descriptor for alert/entity with required integer path id. Extended SCOTCompiler to consume only a single non-negative id equality into the path, reject ambiguous/invalid path predicates, exclude path values from query parameters, and retain unsupported result predicates for local HQL filtering. Added database-native macro resolution, empty-without-request behavior when the path is unresolved, and offline end-to-end tests. Validation: 150 focused SCOT tests pass; full suite 526 passed, 2 skipped, with the same 8 unrelated InstructionSet fake-upstream failures.
close_reason: Implemented and tested the alert entity relationship macro with path-ID extraction and safe empty fallback.

title: Preserve computed Project aliases in data schemas
description: Computed project expressions such as project alertgroup_id = id return the source column schema under id instead of materializing alertgroup_id. A subsequent join cannot resolve the projected join key.
acceptance_criteria: The reported multi-let SCOT query executes project alertgroup_id = id and joins alerts successfully; the projected dataframe and schema both expose alertgroup_id, and an offline end-to-end regression passes.
notes: Fixed computed Project expressions by evaluating NamedExpression with unnest disabled, so the destination path is materialized in both the dataframe and schema rather than returning the source column unchanged. Updated the offline SCOT join regression to the exact multi-let query with project alertgroup_id = id and final Alerts reference. Validation: exact query passes; 345 focused tests pass, 2 skipped; full suite 517 passed, 2 skipped, with the same 8 unrelated InstructionSet fake-upstream failures.
close_reason: Fixed computed Project alias materialization and verified the reported multi-let SCOT join query.

title: Compile and execute joins without optional where clauses
description: The HQL compiler asserts that Join.where is Logic even when a normal join has no where clause. The reported SCOT let/extend/project/join query fails during compilation before execution.
acceptance_criteria: A join with an on clause and no where clause compiles with where=None and executes against mocked SCOT alertgroup and alert inputs, preserving existing optional join-where behavior.
notes: Fixed HqlCompiler.Join so the optional where predicate is only type-checked when present. Reworked Join.gen_optimization to derive distinct join-key rows directly through Summarize instead of the broken temporary Static/Union instruction pipeline, added empty-left handling, and corrected get_right to apply the generated join-key predicate. Added an offline end-to-end regression for the reported let Alert / alertgroup / extend / project / join query, asserting both SCOT request parameters and the joined result. Validation: exact query passes; full suite 517 passed, 2 skipped, with the same 8 unrelated InstructionSet fake-upstream failures.
close_reason: Fixed optional Join.where compilation and end-to-end SCOT join execution.

title: Make SCOT endpoint catalog copyable and pickleable
description: SCOT Endpoint.filters uses MappingProxyType. Context.copy deep-copies symbol-table values containing a selected SCOT database, which raises TypeError: cannot pickle mappingproxy during compilation of repeated database/index expressions.
acceptance_criteria: A selected SCOT database and its endpoint can be deep-copied and pickled without errors; filter metadata remains protected from accidental mutation; the reported compilation path and focused tests pass.
notes: Kept endpoint filter metadata read-only but made Endpoint safe for engine copying and Python pickle. Endpoint.__deepcopy__ returns the immutable instance, __reduce__ serializes filters as a plain dict, and __post_init__ reconstructs a fresh mapping proxy. Added tests for Context.copy with a selected SCOT adapter, endpoint pickle round-trip, and retained immutability. Validation: 172 focused SCOT tests pass; full suite 516 passed, 2 skipped, with the same 8 unrelated InstructionSet fake-upstream failures.
close_reason: Made immutable SCOT endpoints safe for Context deepcopy and pickle serialization.

title: Fix Extend evaluation on SCOT result tables
description: A SCOT query followed by Extend fails in Data.merge/Table.merge_rows after the API response is converted to HQL data. Reproduce with alertgroup and extend TimeGenerated = todatetime(created), identify the schema/row mismatch, and preserve normal Extend semantics.
acceptance_criteria: The reported SCOT query path evaluates Extend successfully, adds TimeGenerated with datetime values, preserves existing columns and rows, and focused regression tests pass.
notes: Fixed Extend evaluation by materializing NamedExpression results into their destination paths before merging, rather than merging the source field name. Corrected scalar schema stripping so a selected scalar is represented by its HQL type instead of a nested Schema/struct. Added a mocked alertgroup regression for extend TimeGenerated = todatetime(created) that verifies the new datetime and preservation of existing fields. Validation: 331 focused tests pass (2 skipped); full suite 514 passed (2 skipped) with the same 8 unrelated InstructionSet fake-upstream failures.
close_reason: Fixed named Extend assignment and scalar schema unwrapping; added SCOT datetime regression coverage.

title: Fix parsing of SCOT table property selection
description: database('scot').entity fails during parsing instead of resolving entity through the SCOT database adapter. Reproduce the grammar/assembly failure, implement the narrow parser or function-chain fix, and add a regression test under the workspace-y79 epic.
notes: User fixed the grammar and requested no further Java/ANTLR regeneration. Parsing database('scot').entity now succeeds, but the assembled query currently deparses to entity: visitFunctionCallOrPathPathExpression/Path drops the database('scot') receiver. Remaining work is visitor/AST resolution only, without grammar regeneration.

title: Add end-to-end SCOT database contract tests
description: Add a final mocked integration suite that exercises the complete HQL path from YAML configuration and database selection through filter/limit compilation, HTTP dispatch, response conversion, and downstream evaluation of rejected operators. Maintain an endpoint coverage matrix tied to the declarative catalog so new or changed OpenAPI resources cannot silently bypass tests.
design: Use recorded minimal response fixtures derived from docs/scot/openapi.json and an injected fake HTTP session. Keep focused unit tests in the implementation tasks; this bead verifies cross-component contracts, catalog completeness, and representative failure paths. Tests must be deterministic, offline, and safe to run without credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Tests execute representative queries for at least entry, entity, one common domain object, an empty collection, and an endpoint with a distinct response shape if one is included. They assert exact path and parameters, API-key handling, pushed and locally evaluated operations, effective limits, Data/Table names and rows, catalog coverage, and sanitized failures. The relevant test suite passes without network access.

title: Push HQL row limits into supported SCOT endpoints
description: Integrate the HQL Take operator with SCOT endpoints that document a limit query parameter. Compute the effective remote limit from the configured safety cap and all applicable Take operations, honor table-targeted and wildcard limits, and never increase an already smaller limit. Endpoints without limit support must reject the operator for local evaluation.
design: Follow the limit behavior in JSON, Elasticsearch, and SQLite adapters. Keep pagination controls separate from filter fields. Push down only a statically evaluable non-negative integer, clamp it to the configured maximum, and retain non-applicable or unsupported Take operations for downstream execution.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover default and maximum limits, smaller and larger Take values, repeated Takes, zero, invalid values, wildcard targeting, matching and nonmatching table targets, and endpoints without limit support. Generated requests contain the smallest applicable safe limit and rejected operators preserve local HQL semantics.
notes: Implemented endpoint-aware Take pushdown in SCOTCompiler. The emitted API limit is the minimum of configured max_rows and all applicable non-negative integer Take values; table names and wildcards are honored, unsupported/nonmatching/invalid Takes remain for local evaluation. Added Alertgroup request integration coverage and compiler edge-case tests. Validation: 169 focused SCOT tests pass; full suite 513 passed, 2 skipped, with 8 pre-existing failures in tests/Compiler/test_instruction_set.py caused by _FakeUpstream rejection.
close_reason: Implemented and tested endpoint-aware Take-to-limit pushdown.

title: Convert SCOT responses into correctly named HQL Data tables
description: Convert successful endpoint responses into Data containing a Table named for the selected SCOT logical resource. Extract rows from the documented ListResponse result field or an explicitly declared catalog-specific path, preserve nested dictionaries/lists for schema inference, and handle empty result sets without losing table identity. Do not accidentally treat resultCount or totalCount as data rows.
design: Make response extraction descriptor-driven and separate from HTTP transport. Supply an OpenAPI-derived schema where needed so an empty response can still produce a named, usable table. Reject unexpected envelope shapes with endpoint context instead of silently returning empty data.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture tests cover representative SCOT resources including entity and entry, nested values, nullable fields, empty results, malformed envelopes, and any catalog exceptions. Each call returns a Data object containing exactly the expected table name and rows, with count metadata excluded from rows and unexpected shapes raising a clear exception.
notes: Implemented SCOT.eval and descriptor-driven response conversion. The adapter validates the configured result path, rejects malformed envelopes/non-list/non-object rows with endpoint context, excludes count metadata, preserves nested/list/nullable values, and returns the execution Context containing an exactly named table, including empty results. Focused SCOT tests: 100 passed. Full suite currently has 8 unrelated InstructionSet test failures in the shared working tree.
close_reason: Implemented and tested SCOT response conversion and eval.

title: Expose each approved SCOT endpoint as an HQL table selection
description: Implement database table selection and endpoint dispatch for every catalog entry. Selecting an HQL table such as entry or entity must bind the matching descriptor, compiler capabilities, and shared query path without duplicating one method body per endpoint. Unknown or excluded resources must fail clearly before any HTTP request.
design: Use get_variable and the database method/variable conventions already used by HQL databases. Generate or dispatch thin endpoint methods from the declarative catalog. Keep the selected endpoint immutable for one database pipeline and ensure add_index, if supported, follows the same validation path.
acceptance_criteria: Parameterized tests select every approved catalog table and assert its request path; unknown, administration, mutation, export, streaming, and binary-download names are rejected without network access; all endpoint dispatch flows through the shared request helper; adding a catalog entry requires no new transport implementation.
notes: Implemented catalog-driven get_variable/add_index table selection, immutable endpoint binding, and generic dispatch through the shared authenticated request helper. Parameterized tests cover all 27 approved tables plus excluded, unknown, export, and download resources with no network calls on rejection. Full suite: 501 passed, 2 skipped.
close_reason: Implemented and tested catalog-driven SCOT table selection and dispatch.

title: Implement one authenticated SCOT request path
description: Add the shared request method used by every SCOT table operation. It must join normalized base URLs and endpoint paths, attach the SCOT Authorization apikey header, pass compiled parameters through requests, enforce timeout and TLS settings, decode JSON, and translate connection, timeout, non-success status, and malformed-response failures into actionable HQL exceptions.
design: Centralize transport behavior so endpoint methods contain no HTTP duplication. Use an injectable requests Session or callable for deterministic tests and connection reuse. Never place the API key in URLs. Error messages may include method, sanitized URL path, and status but must not include credentials or full sensitive response bodies.
acceptance_criteria: Mocked tests verify URL joining, authorization header, query params, timeout, TLS verification, successful JSON decoding, connection failure, timeout, representative 4xx/5xx statuses, malformed JSON, and secret redaction. All table operations call this path and no test needs a live SCOT server.
notes: Implemented the adapter's sole authenticated JSON GET path with normalized URL joining, Authorization apikey header, requests params encoding, timeout/TLS enforcement, path validation, sanitized transport/status/JSON failures, and injected-session tests. Full suite: 455 passed, 2 skipped.
close_reason: Implemented and tested authenticated SCOT request transport.

title: Document and validate SCOT YAML configuration
description: Provide a minimal SCOT database YAML example adjacent to the SCOT class documentation and in conf.example. Explain required base URL and API key fields plus optional TLS verification, timeout, default page size, and maximum limit. Use unmistakable placeholders and document the expected HQL selection form without embedding a usable credential.
design: Keep the inline example synchronized with the constructor contract from workspace-y79.1 and follow the repository database config shape: database, name, type, conf. Prefer environment or deployment-time secret substitution guidance over checked-in values.
acceptance_criteria: The example loads through Config, instantiates the SCOT adapter when placeholders are replaced, shows at least one valid table query, documents every supported option and default, contains no secret, and is covered by a configuration test that detects drift between the example and implementation.
notes: Added conf.example/dbs/scot/conf.yml with required base_url/api_key placeholders, documented verify_tls/timeout/page_size/max_rows defaults, secret-manager guidance, and a database('scot').entity query. Mirrored the example in the SCOT class docstring and added drift tests that load through Config, verify defaults, replace the key at runtime, and instantiate without network access. Full suite: 503 passed, 2 skipped.
close_reason: Added and validated SCOT example configuration and inline documentation.

title: Validate filter pushdown against each SCOT endpoint schema
description: Make SCOT compilation endpoint-aware by validating every proposed filter against the selected table descriptor. Only documented filter fields may be sent to that endpoint, and control parameters such as skip, limit, and sort are managed separately. Apply OpenAPI type information when formatting values and preserve incompatible filters as rejected HQL operations for downstream local evaluation.
design: Pass endpoint capabilities into the compiler instead of hard-coding resource conditionals. Field validation occurs before mutating compiler state. A mixed AND may push valid terms and reject invalid terms; an OR containing any invalid or unsupported term must remain entirely local to preserve semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Parameterized tests cover the allowed-field set for every catalog entry, fields valid on one endpoint but invalid on another, control-parameter isolation, type mismatches, mixed AND predicates, and atomic OR rejection. No invalid field reaches the generated request parameters and rejected predicates remain evaluable after remote results are returned.
notes: Bound SCOTCompiler to immutable endpoint descriptors. It validates fields and declared boolean/date-time/string transport types before serialization, isolates skip/limit/sort controls, permits partial AND pushdown, rejects invalid OR branches atomically, and never mutates state for rejected filters. Parameterized coverage checks every catalog field. Full suite: 442 passed, 2 skipped.
close_reason: Implemented and tested endpoint-aware SCOT filter validation.

title: Define the OpenAPI-derived SCOT table and endpoint catalog
description: Inventory docs/scot/openapi.json and define the approved read-only logical tables. Each table descriptor must record its HQL name, GET collection path, allowed filter parameters and types, response schema/result extraction, and support for skip, limit, and sort. Include domain search/list resources that return tabular JSON; explicitly exclude users, roles, API keys, settings, permissions, login/logout, health, firehose, mutation routes, singleton relationship actions, exports, and file downloads.
design: Keep the catalog declarative so endpoint-specific methods, validation, and response naming share one source of truth. Prefer collection endpoints returning ListResponse models. Document any approved exception such as a non-ListResponse JSON collection and require a fixture for its shape. Do not infer writable API behavior from this catalog.
acceptance_criteria: The catalog has a unique stable HQL name for every included table; every path and parameter exists in the checked-in OpenAPI document; every included response is demonstrably convertible to rows; excluded administration, streaming, binary, and mutation operations cannot be selected; catalog validation tests fail on duplicate names, missing paths, or unsupported response shapes.
notes: Implemented a declarative 27-table catalog in Hql/Database/SCOTCatalog.py with immutable endpoint/filter/control/response descriptors. Added OpenAPI drift validation and tests for the allowlist, exclusions, duplicates, missing paths, controls, filter types, and response shapes. Validation: 8 catalog tests pass; full suite 360 passed, 2 skipped. Repository compileall remains blocked by the pre-existing Kusto.py syntax defect tracked in workspace-qnn.
close_reason: Implemented and validated the OpenAPI-derived SCOT endpoint catalog.

title: Compile supported HQL filter logic into SCOT search parameters
description: Implement the SCOT compiler that consumes HQL Where expressions and produces SCOT search parameters through the URL serializer. Cover equality and inequality, range/between predicates, representable multi-value predicates, conjunctions, and safe negation. Preserve the compiler accepted/rejected contract so unsupported functions, regexes, cross-field OR expressions, or non-static values remain available for local HQL evaluation.
design: Model behavior after existing Lucene and QueryDSL compilers: preprocess first, split only semantically safe AND branches, and reject an entire OR branch when partial pushdown would change results. Compilation should be deterministic and side-effect free until add_op records accepted filters.
acceptance_criteria: Compiler tests verify each supported predicate, multiple compatible where clauses, safe partial AND pushdown, atomic OR rejection, unsupported expressions, and an empty filter set. Accepted expressions yield the documented SCOT parameter grammar; rejected expressions are structurally equivalent to the uncompiled remainder and are never included in remote parameters.
notes: Implemented SCOTCompiler with side-effect-free filter compilation and state mutation only through add_op. Supports scalar/negated equality, same-field OR and multivalue lists, between/not-between ranges, safe atomic Not, partial AND pushdown, atomic cross-field OR rejection, conflict preservation, and deterministic parameters. Full suite: 436 passed, 2 skipped.
close_reason: Implemented and tested SCOT filter compilation and rejection semantics.

title: Implement SCOT URL query-value serialization
description: Create the reusable compiler/serializer layer for converting HQL literal values into SCOT query parameter values. Support strings, integers, floats, booleans, datetimes, negated values, ranges, and multi-value lists using the syntax documented on SCOT search endpoints. Escape leading SCOT control characters and leave final percent encoding to a standards-based URL encoder or requests params handling.
design: Keep value serialization independent of endpoint selection. Produce a deterministic parameter mapping rather than concatenating raw URL strings. Preserve UTC datetime meaning, avoid double encoding, and explicitly reject nested values or expression types that SCOT cannot represent.
acceptance_criteria: Tests demonstrate scalar, datetime, negation, range, list, reserved-character, Unicode, empty-value, and unsupported-type behavior. Generated parameters round-trip through URL encoding without injection, double encoding, or loss of SCOT syntax, and unsupported values are returned as rejected compiler input rather than silently changed.
notes: Implemented SCOTSerializer with deterministic scalar, UTC datetime, negation, range, and flat list grammar; leading control escaping; delimiter/injection safeguards; URL-encoder separation; and explicit rejected-input results. Added coverage for empty values, Unicode, reserved characters, double encoding, nested/unsupported types, and non-finite floats. Full suite: 425 passed, 2 skipped.
close_reason: Implemented and tested SCOT query-value serialization.

title: Scaffold the registered SCOT database adapter and configuration contract
description: Add the SCOT Database subclass under Hql/Database, export it from the package, and register the SCOT type with the existing Context registry. Define and validate the configuration contract for base URL, API key, TLS verification, timeout, default page size, and maximum row limit. Normalize the base URL once and initialize compiler, selected-table state, and supported methods without making a network call during construction.
design: Follow the SQLite, Elasticsearch, and Splunk lifecycle patterns. Read settings from config["conf"], raise ConfigException for missing or invalid required values, keep credentials private, and make request transport injectable or mockable. Constructor defaults must be safe: TLS verification enabled, finite timeout, and bounded result count.
acceptance_criteria: SCOT is resolvable through database("name") when type is SCOT; valid configuration constructs without network access; missing base URL or API key and invalid timeout/limit values produce clear ConfigException messages; normalized configuration and safe defaults are covered by tests; credentials are excluded from to_dict, repr, logs, and exceptions.
notes: Added registered SCOT adapter scaffold with normalized HTTP(S) base URL, required private API key, TLS verification, finite timeout, bounded page/max-row settings, selected-endpoint state, injectable requests session, and secret-safe to_dict/repr behavior. Added construction, registry/database() resolution, defaults, validation, no-network, and redaction tests. Full suite: 393 passed, 2 skipped.
close_reason: Implemented and tested the registered SCOT adapter configuration contract.

title: Implement SCOT as a database using API docs @docs/scot
description: Implement a read-only SCOT 4 database adapter from docs/scot/openapi.json (SCOT 4.7.1). Register SCOT as an HQL database, expose approved JSON collection endpoints as logical tables, push supported HQL filters and row limits into SCOT query parameters, execute authenticated requests, and return named HQL Data/Table objects. Initial scope excludes mutation endpoints, authentication and administration resources, streaming and binary-download endpoints, and operations that cannot produce tabular JSON.
design: Use four layers: an endpoint catalog derived from OpenAPI; a URL value serializer; an endpoint-aware SCOT compiler that accepts only safely representable operators; and a SCOT database transport/response adapter. Endpoint descriptors own the path, logical table name, permitted filter fields, response model/result path, and pagination capability. Unsupported operators remain rejected for normal downstream HQL evaluation. HTTP tests use mocks and fixtures so no live SCOT instance or credentials are required.
acceptance_criteria: A configured database("scot") can select every approved SCOT table, compile supported where/take operations into valid request parameters, fetch through one authenticated request path, and return Data containing correctly named tables. Unsupported fields/operators are not sent remotely. Unit and mocked integration tests cover registration, configuration, compiler semantics, endpoint scope, pagination, response conversion, empty results, and HTTP failures. No secret appears in source, fixtures, logs, or error messages.
notes: Planning assumptions: phase one is read-only and targets authenticated JSON collection endpoints suitable for tabular queries. The exact allowlist is finalized in workspace-y79.4 from the checked-in SCOT 4.7.1 OpenAPI document. Relationship/singleton endpoints are not separate tables unless the catalog task records and tests a clear tabular use case. Unsupported pushdown is preserved for local HQL evaluation rather than changing query semantics.

close_reason: Added concise inline docstrings to all 37 Hql/Functions classes; syntax and AST coverage checks pass.

title: Add explicit Linux ARM64 Rollup dependency
description: Frontend production builds fail because npm omits Rollup's Linux ARM64 optional native package. Declare it explicitly and verify npm run build.
acceptance_criteria: package.json and package-lock.json declare the Linux ARM64 Rollup package and npm run build succeeds.
notes: The reported TS2688 errors are from an incomplete node_modules: all nine referenced @types package directories exist but contain no package.json, and zero @types packages are populated. No additional type declarations are needed in package.json. Recovery requires rm -rf node_modules followed by npm ci --include=optional and npm run build on a host with registry connectivity. Current execution environment cannot fetch either npm registry.

title: Keep post-join SCOT filters after joins and speed fan-out
description: The optimizer hoisted post-join filters such as status and type_name ahead of SCOT joins, causing them to run against alertgroup rows where those entity columns do not exist. Treat joins as row/schema mutation barriers. Keep concurrent SCOT fan-out under the 10 requests/second limit.
acceptance_criteria: Filters on status and type_name remain after the entity join, return matching entity rows, are not sent to the alertgroup API, and focused regression tests pass.
notes: Corrected the initial diagnosis: status and type_name are valid entity result fields. Join descriptors now set row_mutable so row-reducing filters cannot be hoisted across a join. Removed the alertgroup-specific filter workaround. Relationship fan-out remains concurrent under a sliding-window 10/sec limiter. Focused SCOT suite: 158 passed; full suite: 534 passed, 2 skipped, with 8 unrelated existing InstructionSet failures.
close_reason: Fixed optimizer join barrier and validated post-join entity filters.

title: Return SCOT alert entities and limit API calls to 10/sec
description: database('scot').index('alert').macro('entity') returns no rows for alert 42853281 even though SCOT has entities. Ensure scalar and join/fan-out entity requests return results, and throttle SCOT API calls to 10 requests/second.
notes: Relationship responses now expose the queried alert id as id and preserve the SCOT entity id as entity_id, enabling join Entities on id. Added resolved request metadata, configurable default rate limit of 10 requests/sec, example config, and tests including alert 42853281. Focused SCOT suite: 158 passed.
close_reason: Implemented and validated entity relationship joins and SCOT request throttling.

title: Provide static Polars runtime wheels for Linux and Windows x86_64
description: Build Linux x86_64 and Windows x86_64 CPython 3.14t polars-runtime-32 wheels through .github/workflows/build-wheels.yml rather than compiling Polars in local development environments. Publish the wheels to the polars-bin release, then update pyproject.toml and uv.lock so both platforms select the prebuilt assets.
design: Extend the existing wheel-build matrix and preserve the explicit manylinux compatibility policy for Linux.
acceptance_criteria: The GitHub Actions workflow builds and smoke-tests Linux x86_64 and Windows x86_64 CPython 3.14t wheels, publishes both to the polars-bin release, and pyproject.toml plus uv.lock select those wheels without invoking a local Cargo build.
notes:
Implemented local workflow support for Linux x86_64 and Windows x86_64. Linux uses ubuntu-24.04 with a manylinux_2_28 wheel assertion; Windows uses windows-2025 with a win_amd64 assertion. Both smoke-test the built wheel, upload an artifact, and honor publish_release. Validation passed with PyYAML, matrix assertions, actionlint 1.7.12, and git diff --check. Hosted build/publish and dependency lock updates remain pending because the workflow is not on GitHub and this checkout has no authenticated GitHub session.
The Linux container path was hardened after the ARM64 build timed out silently: compilation now runs outside the Docker image layer with bounded Cargo concurrency, a mounted target directory, reduced release-profile overhead, offline locked dependencies, resource heartbeats, and explicit exit/OOM diagnostics. The same path applies to Linux x86_64. Hosted validation remains pending.
Hosted x86_64 rerun ce24722 exposed a stale packaged Cargo.lock before compilation. The builder now permits one online lock normalization during cargo fetch, validates the result locked/offline, then performs the runtime compile locked and without networking. Fresh-sdist reproduction passes; hosted rerun remains pending.
close_reason: Resolved: platform wheels are published and dependency configuration now selects the prebuilt assets.

title: Provide a static Polars runtime wheel for Linux ARM64
description: Build the missing Linux ARM64 static polars-runtime-32 wheel through the repository GitHub Actions workflow rather than compiling Polars in the local development environment. Publish or otherwise expose the wheel at the dependency URL used by pyproject.toml, then update pyproject.toml and uv.lock so Linux ARM64 selects it.
acceptance_criteria: pyproject.toml and uv.lock select a compatible prebuilt polars-runtime-32 wheel on Linux ARM64, and uv sync does not invoke Cargo.
notes:
Implemented and committed the initial GitHub Actions build path in ce3cde7. A hosted Linux run then failed manylinux_2_28 validation because maturin compiled on Ubuntu 24.04 and retained GLIBC 2.29-2.39 symbols. The working tree now changes both Linux matrix jobs to build via scripts/Containerfile.polars using the architecture-specific manylinux_2_28 image, while retaining host Python only for smoke testing. Workflow YAML and whitespace validation pass; a hosted rerun remains pending. After publishing the ARM64 asset, add its release URL to pyproject.toml and regenerate uv.lock.
A subsequent hosted ARM64 container build reached Rust compilation but then timed out without a useful terminal error. The working tree now runs Cargo in a runtime container instead of a Dockerfile RUN layer, mounts the multi-GB target directory outside the image snapshot, limits Cargo to two jobs, disables release debug info and thin-LTO, prefetches locked dependencies, builds offline, emits one-minute CPU/memory/disk heartbeats, and reports container exit/OOM/Docker-daemon state. Job and compile-step timeouts are explicit at 180 and 150 minutes. Hosted rerun remains pending.
Hosted rerun ce24722 failed during builder preparation because the published 1.43.2 sdist lockfile requires normalization and cargo fetch --locked refused to change it. Containerfile now allows cargo fetch to normalize the packaged lock once while online, immediately validates it with cargo metadata --locked --offline, and keeps the runtime maturin compile locked and network-isolated. Reproduced successfully against a freshly downloaded sdist: the lock hash changed from 60e2b5c... to 4e3ab82..., then locked/offline metadata passed. Hosted rerun remains pending.
